reason: The supplied proof is valid; the argument explicitly uses that \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\) and that continuous maps pull back closed sets to closed sets.
text:
Since \(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\) is open, \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\). Because \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, the inverse image of every closed subset of \(\mathbb{R}\) is closed in \(X\). Therefore
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\})
\]
is closed in \(X\).
